cases.statement: One person (Table 2 #30 of the SSADHD natural-history cohort), listed in both copies of the same preprint; c.127delC with c.803G > A, labelled compound heterozygosis. No individual clinical description.

people.label: Table 2 #30
people.key_phenotypes: not reported individually (cohort-level data only) (same preprint text as 37503297)

phenotype_specificity.statement: Only cohort-level phenotype data; the cohort was enrolled after genetic confirmation of SSADHD. No statement about testing of other genes.

quotes.quote: Movement disorders were present in 32 (55%) subjects: 30 (52%) had ataxia, 14 (24%) had dyskinesia, and 9 (15%) had dystonia.
After being genetically confirmed with SSADHD, subjects enrolled in the natural history study undergo a series of clinical and laboratory assessments biennially.

in_trans.statement: Other allele c.803G > A (G268E), stated in Table 2 with the label "Compound heterozygosis". Parental testing and phase are not reported.

variant_type_and_mechanism.statement: Single-nucleotide deletion in the first coding exon causing a frameshift (predicted p.(Gln43SerfsTer48)); the paper places it in the mitochondrial targeting sequence. The paper describes the disease as autosomal recessive and states that biallelic premature stops give no functional protein.

quotes.quote: | c.127delC | Q43SfsX47 | Exon 1 | Mitochondrial targeting sequence |

Succinic semialdehyde dehydrogenase deficiency (SSADHD) (OMIM #271980) is a rare (prevalent in ~ 1/460,000^1) inherited metabolic disorder caused by autosomal recessive inheritance of ALDH5A1 sequence variants^2.
If the genetic variant (insertion or deletion) results in a premature stop codon on both alleles, a functional SSADH protein would not be synthesized.

computational_predictions.statement: No variant-level score is given for this frameshift. The authors' structural model assigns this genotype to "Hemizygote G268E homotetramers" with a catalysis effect (a prediction from the other allele).

authors_classification.statement: Authors list c.127delC among eight previously unreported variants and make a blanket statement covering all 32 cohort variants.

quotes.quote: eight of which were previously unreported (c.104_127 del, c.127delC, c.870 + 1G > T, 6p22.3 deletion, c.644_647delTGGG, c.1558G > C, c.755G > A, and c.1388del) (Table 1)
This study’s findings determined that the 32 allelic variants (eight of which are novel), present in 41 unique allelic combinations (Table 1) in 58 SSADHD participants, were pathogenic.

concerns: PMIDs 37503297 and 37962671 carry the same Research Square preprint text (DOI 10.21203/rs.3.rs-3111263/v1); 37962671 states a version was later published in Human Genetics. The two rows are one person counted once (same identity), not independent observations.

The person appears only as a numbered row in a genotype table of a natural-history cohort; there is no individual case description, sex, age or phenotype for this row. The cohort is 58 individuals from 50 families, so some rows are relatives, but the paper does not say which.
Zygosity is given only as a table label; the paper does not report parental testing or how phase was established.

Protein notation differs in style only: the paper writes Q43SfsX47, the batch prediction is p.(Gln43SerfsTer48); the batch marks the protein check as agreeing. The panel may wish to confirm the frameshift length.
No transcript is stated in this paper.
notes_for_panel: Evidence is limited to a genotype-table row in a cohort preprint; the blanket author statement covers all 32 cohort variants and is not specific to this variant.
